items.name: Freedom Trail
items.blurb: A 2.5-mile red-brick trail linking 16 historic sites through downtown Boston.

items.name: Faneuil Hall Marketplace
items.blurb: Historic market hall with food stalls, shops, and street performers.

items.name: Boston Public Garden
items.blurb: America's first public botanical garden — swan boats and the Make Way for Ducklings statues.

items.name: Museum of Fine Arts
items.blurb: One of the largest art museums in the US, with an encyclopedic collection.

items.name: New England Aquarium
items.blurb: Harborside aquarium centered on a four-story ocean tank.

items.name: Fenway Park
items.blurb: Home of the Red Sox and the oldest ballpark still in use in MLB.

items.name: Boston Common
items.blurb: The oldest city park in the US, anchoring the start of the Freedom Trail.

items.name: USS Constitution
items.blurb: The world's oldest commissioned warship still afloat, docked in Charlestown.

items.name: Paul Revere House
items.blurb: Boston's oldest surviving structure, home of the famous midnight rider.

items.name: Boston Tea Party Ships & Museum
items.blurb: Interactive waterfront museum with a reenactment and replica ships.

items.name: Harvard Square
items.blurb: Bookshops, cafes, and Harvard Yard just across the river in Cambridge.

items.name: Quincy Market
items.blurb: Long domed market hall packed with New England food vendors.
